podcast.body: Considered a "stone-cold classic," this album further established Sinéad O'Connor's reputation as one of the most formidable singers globally, characterized by her distinctive voice and perspective. "Her first two albums, The Line and the Cobra from 1987, and I do not want what I haven't got from 1990, are stone-cold classics."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The 100 Greatest Rock Moments of the Millennium So Far - Part 3: (80-71)

podcast.body: Released on March 20, 1990, this album was a massive global success, shooting to number one worldwide and selling millions, earning four Grammy nominations. Engineer Chris Birkett was brought in last-minute to produce it after Sinead walked out on the initial producer, Nellee Hooper, after two days, despite the record company initially not wanting to release it, deeming it "too personal." Sinead's contract gave her complete creative control, forcing its release. The title comes from a spiritualist session where she contacted her deceased mother, signifying her mother's spirit wasn't seeking forgiveness. There were two album covers; the European edition featured an angry, screaming shot, while the North American division opted for a more demure photo from the same session. "She forced them to release it."

podcast.body: This album was "very good" musically, but O'Connor's public behavior overshadowed its quality. It was nominated for four Grammys, which she boycotted. "I do not want what I haven't got was very good."

podcast.body: This album won the first-ever Grammy Award for an alternative artist in 1991, signaling the Grammy Awards' recognition of alternative music. "And the winner was Shaneo Connor for her, I do not want what I haven't gone album."

podcast.body: Sinéad O'Connor's album "I Do Not Want What I Haven't Got" won the very first Grammy Award in the "Alternative Album" category in 1991. This victory solidified her place in alternative music history and marked a new era for Grammy recognition of the genre. "And the winner was Shanato Conner for her I do not want what I haven't got album."
